title: arxiv_2304.04437v1
universal_lens: Monocular 3D human pose estimation integrates 2D joint detection with scene geometry via partial field registration, enabling kinematic reconstruction under affine constraints. Partial field registration via vanishing point constraints enables 3D skeleton lifting with geometric consistency.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on 2D pose likelihood conditioned on calibrated scene geometry; conformal prediction bounds uncertainty in 3D kinematics across camera views. Bayesian calibration update using vanishing point priors and 2D reprojection consistency for robust GSI tracking.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps 2D joint trajectories to 3D state transitions through geometric constraints; state-transition graphs encode athlete motion dynamics with temporal coherence. Situation-aware state transitions driven by 3D ray-casting and temporal frame consistency in GSE motion modeling.

primitives.name: Kinematic Reconstruction Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Through joint optimization of 3D pose estimation and camera calibration, we demonstrate the successful extraction of 3D running kinematics on a 400m track.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal continuity of motion and stable camera setup.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion is non-rigid or camera instability occurs.

primitives.name: Partial Field Registration
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use a constructive method to find a complete set of valid camera calibrations that are consistent with just a single vanishing point derived from lanes in the image [3].
primitives.assumptions: Vanishing point from lane markings defines a constraint set of valid camera calibrations; field registration is partial due to limited field visibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When only a subset of the field is visible, e.g., small portions of a 400m track, full registration becomes infeasible.

layer2.mapping: The set of valid camera calibrations forms an isomorphic space to the geometric constraints imposed by lane alignment in 2D image space.
layer2.telemetry: Reprojection error between 2D skeleton and 3D lifted skeleton.

primitives.name: Ray-Casting 3D Lifting
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1(d), we use explicit knowledge about the 3D geometry of the current frame to cast a ray through the image and lift a 2D skeleton into 3D.
primitives.assumptions: Explicit 3D geometry of the scene is known or inferred; 2D skeleton points are projected onto rays to recover 3D positions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When 2D skeleton lacks sufficient depth cues, ray-casting fails without additional geometric context.

layer2.mapping: The kernel of 3D lifting is derived from the inverse projection of 2D points along rays defined by camera calibration and scene geometry.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation of 3D limb configuration from ground truth.

primitives.name: Temporal Consistency Field Derivation

primitives.name: Pose-Guided Field Registration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Discussion In this work, we developed a method for combining 2D HPE and partial sports field registration to determine the 3D locations of joints and thereby the kinematics of athletes.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes availability of accurate 2D joint detections and geometric constraints of the sports field; requires camera calibration parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates when 2D pose estimators fail to identify sufficient landmarks or when field geometry is partially occluded.

primitives.name: Partial Field Registration
primitives.verbatim_quote: In many sports (e.g., soccer), the field has an extent that does not allow to perform typical approaches of sports field registration in this case: not enough area of the field is visible.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes knowledge of only a subset of field markers (e.g., straight lane lines) rather than full field layout, enabling robustness to partial occlusions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when insufficient marker lines are visible, requiring fallback to alternative geometric priors or optical flow.

primitives.name: Zoomed-In Monocular Reconstruction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our work focuses on a scenario in which the camera is zoomed-in on the athlete at a level that kinematics are derivable from that view.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down at wide-angle views where parallax errors become significant due to the small subject-to-field ratio.

It addresses the core challenge of lifting 2D joint detections into 3D space without explicit depth sensors. The methodology hinges on leveraging known scene geometry—specifically, line markings on sports fields—to perform camera calibration and scene reconstruction. This approach circumvents the need for expensive multi-view setups while maintaining accuracy through partial field registration. The integration of 2D pose estimation with scene geometry enables robust tracking of athletic motion, particularly useful for biomechanical analysis and performance monitoring. The paper also highlights limitations of current monocular 3D HPE techniques, demonstrating that synthetic datasets generated in Unreal Engine 5 reveal gaps in real-world applicability. By combining advances in both domains, the authors propose a scalable solution for generating large-scale kinematic datasets essential for modern sports analytics.
